apis.name: restart
apis.signature: async def restart(self, *, at: str | None = None, restore: bool = True, seed_states: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> None
apis.semantics: Tears the config entry down (unload), captures current states of the entry's restorable entities (switches, select), seeds mock_restore_cache with them (or seed_states overrides), re-runs async_setup on the same entry, and re-wins the fake cover services. Timeline is preserved so tests can assert 'no duplicate close after restart' / 'catch-up close fired on setup'. Shade states persist in hass.states across the restart, as in real HA. Also generalize/document create(start_at=...) for daytime starts (needed for first-refresh-positions).
apis.implementation_notes: Factor the tail of SimHouse.create() (setup + _register_services() re-win + coordinator re-fetch) into async _setup_entry(); restart() = optional advance_to(at) -> collect states via er.async_entries_for_config_entry -> async_unload -> mock_restore_cache -> await self._setup_entry(). Unblocks: catchup-close-after-restart, switch-restore, first-refresh-positions.

apis.name: set_options
apis.semantics: Merges option_changes into entry.options via hass.config_entries.async_update_entry, waits for the entry reload to complete, re-registers the fake cover services (reload re-runs the hub bootstrap which steals them), and refreshes self.coordinator. Models 'user edits options in the UI at 14:00' as one call; replaces the private house._register_services() reach in test_regressions.py.
apis.implementation_notes: ~10 lines reusing _setup_entry-style re-win; migrate the existing test_regressions.py caller inside this package (shared-file rule). Unblocks: end-time-rearm-on-change, reload variants of first-refresh/interpolation/inverse/midnight-end-time.

apis.name: multi-day sun regeneration (SimSunData.regenerate_for)
apis.signature: class SimSunData(FakeSunData): def regenerate_for(self, date: pd.Timestamp) -> None  # no new public SimHouse API
apis.semantics: tick() detects a local-date change and calls sun_data.regenerate_for(new_date), recomputing times/solar_azimuth/solar_elevation/date IN PLACE (calculation.py holds a reference to the single patched instance) so day-two sunset()/sunrise(), solar-time sensors, and forecasts are correct. DST days need no extra API — pick a transition date (e.g. 2026-03-08 America/Denver) and advance_to across it.
apis.implementation_notes: Subclass in harness.py; leave golden_lib.FakeSunData untouched for characterization determinism. Fix while here: _local() uses pytz.localize on naive times — catch AmbiguousTimeError/NonExistentTimeError and take the fold, or transition-day tests crash at 02:30. Unblocks: day-rollover-clears-overrides (assertable via next-morning auto_moves), solar-day-table-regen.

apis.name: shade_goes_unavailable / shade_returns
apis.signature: async def shade_goes_unavailable(self, entity_id: str) -> None; async def shade_returns(self, entity_id: str) -> None
apis.semantics: Write the 'unavailable' state / restore the real state with a device context; service calls to an unavailable shade keep raising as today. The hand-rolled version in test_regressions.py migrates onto this public API inside this package.
apis.implementation_notes: Part of the FakeShade fault API (audit E4).

apis.name: jam
apis.semantics: Shade stops mid-travel at an interpolated intermediate position, never lands, no landing report ever; an arrival-poll (homeassistant.update_entity) reports the stuck position — distinguishing jam from drop_landing_report.
apis.implementation_notes: FakeShade gains jammed: bool; jam() computes the interpolated position from elapsed/travel_seconds; _land() skipped while jammed; handle_update_entity reports the stuck position.

apis.name: drop_landing_report
apis.semantics: The next landing is silent: the shade DOES reach its target but the state report is swallowed; the true position surfaces only on the next poll. Exercises poll-on-silence / pending-snap retry paths.
apis.implementation_notes: FakeShade.drop_next_landing: bool; _land() updates position but skips _write_shade_state once.

apis.name: strip_position_attr
apis.signature: def strip_position_attr(self, entity_id: str, on: bool = True) -> None
apis.semantics: While on, the shade's state writes omit current_position/current_tilt_position — models covers that report no position. Drives unknown-position-commands-anyway and no-position-no-latch.

apis.name: fail_next_command
apis.signature: def fail_next_command(self, entity_id: str, exc: Exception | None = None) -> None
apis.semantics: The fake cover.set_cover_position handler raises once (default HomeAssistantError) for this shade, before recording any travel — proving the update loop survives, other covers still get commanded, and the failed cover is re-commanded later. This is what de-vacuates the pending-end-snap retry test.
apis.implementation_notes: FakeShade.fail_next: Exception | None consumed at the top of handle_set_position.

apis.name: eid / entity / sensor_value / sensor_attr
apis.signature: def eid(self, domain: str, key: str) -> str; def entity(self, domain: str, key: str) -> State | None; def sensor_value(self, key: str = 'cover_position') -> str; def sensor_attr(self, key: str, attr: str)
apis.semantics: Resolve the entry's entities by unique-id suffix through the entity registry (never hard-coding sim_house_-slugged entity_ids) and read their states/attributes (e.g. cover_position state, move_blocked_by, intent, decision_trace) as one-liners.
apis.implementation_notes: Pure additions to SimHouse via er.async_entries_for_config_entry matched on unique-id suffix.

apis.name: toggle / press / select_option
apis.signature: async def toggle(self, key: str, on: bool) -> None; async def press(self, key: str = 'reset_manual_override') -> None; async def select_option(self, key: str, option: str) -> None
apis.semantics: Flip the entry's switches / press its buttons / set its select through REAL HA service calls with a user Context — pinning switch/button/select semantics at the entity boundary instead of poking coordinator.control_toggle. Largest single unblock: 10 critical/high gaps (gate-precedence, control-toggle-off/on/clears, climate-mode-switch, manual-toggle-off, reset-button, aux toggles, position-sensor reads).

apis.name: aux climate entities: set_lux / set_irradiance / set_outside_temp (+ create() extension)
apis.signature: create(climate={... lux=450, irradiance=300, outside_temp=28.0, lux_threshold=1000, irradiance_threshold=300, presence_domain='zone'|'binary_sensor'|'input_boolean'|'device_tracker'}); async def set_lux(self, value: float | str); async def set_irradiance(self, value: float | str); async def set_outside_temp(self, value: float | str)
apis.semantics: When the climate dict names them, the harness creates sensor.sim_lux / sensor.sim_irradiance / sensor.sim_outdoor_temp and wires CONF_LUX_ENTITY/CONF_IRRADIANCE_ENTITY/CONF_OUTSIDETEMP_ENTITY (+ thresholds) into the entry. Setters accept strings so 'unavailable'/garbage drive resilience scenarios. presence_domain parameterizes the presence entity's domain for the presence-entity-domains gap.
apis.implementation_notes: Mirror the existing TEMP/PRESENCE/WEATHER pattern in create() and the three existing setters; ~25 lines.

apis.name: hold_timers / release_timers
apis.signature: def hold_timers(self) -> None; async def release_timers(self) -> None
apis.semantics: Between hold and release, tick() advances the freezer, sun state, and shade travel but does NOT fire time listeners — so a point-in-time listener (the end-time close) scheduled for 20:00 is delivered late, e.g. at 20:40, on release. Reproduces 'HA delivered the callback late' and, with set_options, 'end time moved after arming'.
apis.implementation_notes: self._timers_held flag checked in tick(); release_timers() = async_fire_time_changed(hass, self.now) + block_till_done; ~8 lines. Deliberately minimal — no per-listener targeting.

apis.name: tilt fidelity (FakeShade.tilt + set_cover_tilt_position routing)
apis.signature: FakeShade gains tilt: int = 100; separate handle_set_tilt service handler; def position(self, entity_id, *, tilt: bool = False) -> int
apis.semantics: Split the currently-mirrored fields: set_cover_tilt_position moves the tilt field, set_cover_position moves position; _write_shade_state reports each attribute from its own field. A tilt house then proves commands go through set_cover_tilt_position and manual detection reads current_tilt_position. (Audit claim was slightly stale: current_tilt_position is already written but mirrors position.)
apis.implementation_notes: Register handle_set_tilt sharing the travel/timeline code with a field='tilt' parameter; ~20 lines.

apis.name: golden_lib.patch_sun_data
apis.semantics: THE single test-side place that knows SunData's import path (patch('custom_components.adaptive_cover.calculation.SunData', return_value=sun_data)). All five call sites migrate onto it: harness._patch, root conftest.mock_sun_data, golden_lib, truth-table generator. A refactor then breaks one line, not five. The real production seam (a sun_data_factory hook) is the refactor's own first commit and swaps only this helper's body.
apis.implementation_notes: Shared-file work; lives in golden_lib.py; part of this sequential package.

apis.name: golden_lib.is_integration_context
apis.semantics: THE single test-side place that knows integration-issued commands are marked via coordinator._our_context_ids; harness._actor_for migrates onto it. The public coordinator.is_own_context(ctx) method is the refactor's own first commit and swaps only this helper's body.
apis.implementation_notes: Shared-file work; documented as a known coupling until the refactor lands the public seam.

apis.name: mutation-set runner
apis.signature: tests/mutation_set/*.patch + tests/mutation_set/run_mutations.sh (apply -> pytest -> revert, per patch, per tier)
apis.semantics: The 43 mutations below committed as one-line patch files with a runner that reports the kill matrix (which tier killed which mutation), making the kill-rate a reproducible number, not an anecdote.

Files owned by this package: tests/simulation/harness.py, tests/simulation/conftest.py, tests/characterization/golden_lib.py (seam helpers only), tests/conftest.py (mock_sun_data migration), tests/simulation/test_regressions.py (migrate private-reach call sites), tests/simulation/README.md, tests/mutation_set/*, tests/simulation/test_harness_extensions.py.

migration_package.why: Already on public seams (engine evaluate/models, SimHouse surfaces, hass states/services/registries). test_purity.py stays as a structural guard.

behavior_tier: A test is behavior-tier iff it touches the code only through the Refactor Contract seams: (1) engine.evaluate(config, sun, ctx, climate=None) -> Decision, the engine/models.py dataclasses and field names, the Intent enum, and the documented geometry functions gamma/valid_elevation/sunlit_top/tilt_percentage/profile_angle (trace strings semi-stable, pinned by goldens); (2) the config surface — const.py CONF_* keys and defaults, entry data/options shapes, options-over-data merge rule; (3) the entity surface — unique-id/entity-id scheme, sensor states and attributes (intent, decision_trace, move_blocked_by, forecast_today, manual_controlled, last/next-change formats), switch/select/button/binary-sensor semantics, RestoreEntity behavior; (4) the service surface — outbound cover.set_cover_position / cover.set_cover_tilt_position / homeassistant.update_entity calls (targets, values, timing) and inbound adaptive_cover.get_forecast + settings services; (5) SunData's public API (sun.py) as pinned by test_regression_sun_data_public_api_intact.

IN the tier: tests/simulation/** (SimHouse drives a real config entry through HA surfaces; its two internal couplings — coordinator._our_context_ids and patch('...calculation.SunData') — are centralized behind the golden_lib.is_integration_context / patch_sun_data helpers by the harness package, the only sanctioned exceptions until the refactor's first commit makes them public seams; the vacuous test_symptoms end-time-retry test is replaced by wp7's real one).

IN the tier: tests/characterization/test_golden_days.py + goldens/*.txt and test_climate_truth_table.py + climate_truth_table.json — counting only AFTER the migration package re-points golden_lib/truth_table_lib at engine.evaluate() with byte-identical outputs (the no-diff is itself the migration's verification).

IN the tier: tests/engine/** tests that call evaluate() or the documented geometry functions with models.py dataclasses; test_purity.py stays as a structural guard (not behavior, never a false positive).

IN the tier: root entity-surface tests that set up a real entry and assert only via hass.states, entity service calls, registries, and mocked cover services: test_service_calls.py, test_hub.py, test_provenance.py, test_change_settings.py, test_night_born_entries.py, test_add_entry.py, test_init.py, test_one_page_options.py, test_config_flow.py, test_forecast_and_trace.py, test_live_tunables.py::TestNumberEntities/TestGateVisibility, and the entity-level half of test_smoothing_and_privacy.py — plus the new wp9/wp10 files.

EXCLUDED (implementation tier — a refactor may freely break these; zero weight in the acceptance gate): tests/characterization/test_coordinator_gating.py; tests/test_coordinator.py (manager built directly, private method bound onto a MagicMock); tests/test_calculation.py (legacy-adapter constructors); tests/test_button.py (MagicMock coordinator encoding wait_for_target/TARGET_TIMEOUT); tests/test_smoothing_and_privacy.py::TestQuietHours/::TestMoveBudget (import make_coordinator); test_regression_fixes.py's direct ClimateCoverData / cover-constructor tests (its SunData tests stay behavior-tier); and any assert anywhere on coordinator.control_toggle, coordinator.manager.is_cover_manual, coordinator.data internals, or _-prefixed attributes.

Acceptance criterion (the deletion drill, run at refactor time): with the implementation tier entirely deleted (git rm the excluded files/classes), the behavior tier passes on trunk and kills 100% of the standard mutation set. That drill is the definition of done for 'refactor-safe'.

acceptance.kill_rate_bar: Behavior tier kills 43/43 (100%) — non-negotiable; a surviving mutation is a missing work package, not a waiver. tests/simulation/ ALONE must kill all coordinator-lifecycle mutations: groups A, B, C, F (M01–M18, M35–M39) plus M43 — coordinator internals are what the refactor reshapes most, and the sim is the only tier that survives that reshaping by construction. Group G's entity mutations (M40–M42) may be killed by sim or the entity-surface behavior tests. Engine mutations (D, E: M19–M34) may be killed by any of goldens / truth table / tests/engine — the evaluate() seam is itself frozen. Baseline for comparison: today the sim kills 5/24 (21%) and 4/24 were killed by nothing; those four (M14, M15, M16, M36) are first-priority and are each named in a package's acceptance (wp4, wp5, wp7). Kill rates are measured with the tests/mutation_set/ patch files + apply-run-revert runner landed by the harness package, so the number is reproducible.
acceptance.notes: SCHEDULING (fits ~10 parallel agents): Phase 1 — harness-ext package runs ALONE as the sole owner of shared files (harness.py, simulation/conftest.py, golden_lib.py seam helpers, root conftest, test_regressions.py call-site migration, README, mutation_set/, its smoke file); wp1-engine-geometry, wp9-entity-surfaces, and wp10-hub-behavior may run concurrently with it since they touch no shared file. Phase 2 — the remaining seven packages in parallel, each confined to its one new test file, priority tier A: wp2, wp3, wp4; tier B: wp5, wp6; tier C: wp7, wp8. Phase 3 — the migration package runs sequentially last (it edits many existing shared test files): golden/truth-table driver re-point with byte-identical outputs, assert rewrites, then retirements — each retirement only after the mutation runner shows the named replacement package killing that file's mutations — finishing with the section-defining deletion drill. CONSTRAINTS: tests only; production code must not change — a package that discovers a real production bug reports it instead of fixing (one known suite bug is pre-registered: the vacuous test_symptoms end-time-retry test, owned by wp7). DEFERRED TO THE REFACTOR'S FIRST COMMIT (spec for those agents): public coordinator.is_own_context(ctx) and a module-level sun_data_factory hook in calculation.py; until then the two golden_lib helpers are the single sanctioned coupling points. DROPPED WITH REASONS: E10 hub-inclusive sim mode and the §9 fake-service hub delegation (plain-HA wp10 covers those gaps), E11 streamed-position shade, per-listener timer targeting / sub-minute races, blueprint/translations harness support, and the low lovelace-card-registration gap. Gap coverage: 25/25 critical, 24/24 high, 14/14 medium, 2/3 low (lovelace excluded).
